item.title: An empty bus pulled into Ridgland Farms in Wisconsin last week and emerged with more than 150 rescued beagles – who had never felt grass or fresh air in their lives. More than 2,000 beagles had been already rescued from the farm, a controversial biomedical research and breeding facility. CBS News' Adam Yamaguchi got to be there as the remaining dogs – many of them puppies – had their first taste of freedom. Many of the dogs were paralyzed with fear as they finally exited the cages they had been trapped in and entered the unknown world of caring human beings and safety. After protesters tried to break into the facility to rescue the dogs earlier this year, the facility decided to shut down its breeding operations. The remaining beagles were taken to Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Florida, where they will be put up for adoption. #beagles #rescue #dogrescue #dogs | CBS News

item.title: AI should transform the strategy process—but never make the final call, researcher argues
item.description: A practitioner article published in the SMS Explorer, "AI Will Help Formulate Strategy, But Should Never Finish It," by Michael Olenick challenges a growing assumption in the business world: that generative AI can take strategy off executives' plates. As AI tools grow more capable, the debate has shifted from whether AI can contribute to strategy to whether it should lead it. Olenick, drawing on more than two decades of AI-aided strategy research, argues it should not—and explains precisely where the line must be drawn. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: European hedgehogs were brought to New Zealand during the 1800s to help manage garden pests. However, these spiky creatures now pose a grave danger to the country's unique wildlife. They feast on the eggs and young of various native species, significantly impacting fragile ecosystems, particularly those involving ground-nesting birds. As a result, ongoing conservation initiatives are prioritizing hedgehog removal to protect these threatened populations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Dynamic surface reconstruction explains how copper sulfide catalysts tune CO₂ reduction
item.description: Copper sulfide (CuS) catalysts continuously reconstruct their surface during electrochemical CO2 reduction, reports a study from the Institute of Science Tokyo, Japan. By uncovering the mechanism behind the dynamic surface changes that occur during potential-step electrolysis, the researchers revealed how sulfur and oxygen play distinct roles in catalyst activity and product selectivity, paving the way for improved CO2 conversion technologies. Fuente: Phys.org.
